text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Five were killed and 11 injured in riot at Metris prison in Istanbul. The riot was taken under control by the military.
- High-ranking military official says legal action will be taken against ex-interior minister Meral Aksener for claiming she had discovered coup plans.
- State minister responsible for economy and the finance minister said they would fight high inflation.
- Finance minister says that despite the 35 percent pay rise given to civil servants the real rise achieved in salaries is only 22 percent.
- An International Monetary Fund report reveals heavy damage to the economy caused by the former Islamist-led government.
- Foreign Minister Ismail Cem is very optimistic about the improvement of relations with traditional foe Greece after agreement was at the Madrid summit between the two countries.
- A court sentences Selcuk Parsadan to more than 6 years for swindling 5.5 billion lira from government slush fund during conservative Tansu Ciller's premiership.
- President Suleyman Demirel says Turkey was respected at NATO summit following recent government changes.
- New government's portrait of the economy is pessimistic.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz meets army number two.
